Results

Did pinn last longer? No clear difference: pinn did not keep a reliably lower joint-angle error than base after the switch to stairs (mean error on stairs over hip, knee and ankle: base 11.38°, pinn 11.35°; Wilcoxon p = 0.744, rank-biserial r = 0.10, n = 16 people).

The two numbers per model

Error after switch: RMSE (°) over the stairs part, mean over people. Time to fail: median over people of the time (s) until the rolling 2 s error stays above 1.5 × the model's own walking error for 2 s; runs that never fail count as the horizon H = 423 s.

ModelError after switch (°) Time to fail (s)Walking error (°)
hipkneeanklemeanhipkneeanklehipkneeankle
base10.5615.927.6711.381.91.92.88.057.365.07
pinn10.3716.197.4911.351.71.82.27.396.154.70

How to read time to fail: both models cross the threshold 1.7–2.8 s (median per joint) after the switch. That is before the first stair step (each stair recording starts with 2–3 s of walking up to the stairs) and within the network's 1.27 s context across the join between recordings, so it mostly reflects the join and the approach rather than the climbing itself.

Test

Primary endpoint: error after switch averaged over hip, knee and ankle, paired across 16 people (base − pinn). Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.744; rank-biserial r = +0.10; Hodges–Lehmann difference +0.05° (95% bootstrap CI -0.29 to +0.43). Verdict: no clear difference.

Excluded by the pre-registered gyro check: AB06, AB07, AB08, AB16, AB19, AB20. Sensitivity (all 22 people, not the verdict): p = 0.899, r = -0.04.

Around each stair entry

Added after the main result: a strongly physics-constrained model

Not pre-registered. Requested after the main result was known. pinn_strong is the tuned pinn network (lr 0.003, width 64) with a fixed, large physics weight λ = 0.1, chosen from walking-only loss scales and not tuned. Compared with base by the same test on the same 16 people: base had the lower error on stairs (Wilcoxon p = 0.044, rank-biserial r = -0.57, Hodges–Lehmann difference base − pinn_strong -0.77°, 95% CI -1.46 to -0.09).
